{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABfFTMOA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhI2VGw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 377, "title": "Support safe multiline voice insertion in Lexical and Draft.js editors", "body": "## Problem

Remaining compatibility work from #375, split out of the partial implementation in #376. Chromium browser editing experiments with Lexical 0.38.2 and Draft.js 0.11.7 lost existing content or line breaks when using insertText/insertParagraph/insertLineBreak for multiline text. The shared strategy currently rejects segments containing CR/LF for those roots before editing, retaining them as definitely uninserted for explicit recovery/copy. Single-line segments persist in the real application models and support Undo/Redo.

## First step: read upstream editor source and establish a safe external insertion path

**Investigate the official open-source implementations before changing the rejection guard or adding site-specific workarounds.** Both Lexical and Draft.js support multiline documents internally; determine *how their actual DOM input/paste handlers convert browser editing actions into editor-state updates*, and why the current external insertion sequence loses existing text or line breaks.

1. **Lexical:** inspect [facebook/lexical](https://github.com/facebook/lexical) (target the version used by our fixtures, 0.38.2), especially `beforeinput`, `input`, paste/clipboard handling, text insertion and paragraph/line-break commands, selection restoration, transactions and Undo history. Trace how a normal multi-line paste or typing sequence reaches the internal editor state.
2. **Draft.js:** inspect [facebookarchive/draft-js](https://github.com/facebookarchive/draft-js) (fixture 0.11.7), especially `editOnBeforeInput`, paste handling, `EditorState`, `Modifier`, `ContentState`, `ContentBlock`, fragment insertion and Undo. Trace the real edit/paste path for multiple blocks.
3. For **each** editor, distinguish APIs callable *inside an application that owns the editor instance* from editing actions available to an **external Chrome extension content script**. Our extension does **not** own the page's Lexical editor instance or Draft.js `EditorState`; direct calls to internal commands are not a valid general strategy unless there is a documented, safely accessible host interface. Respect Chrome isolated worlds and existing permission/security boundaries. Do not inject page-world code just to discover private editor objects.
4. Investigate which genuine browser editing operations are interpreted correctly (where applicable, `execCommand('insertText')`, `insertParagraph`, `insertLineBreak`, and paste-like browser behavior). Verify real state persistence, selection, line breaks, re-render and Undo/Redo. **Deprecated `execCommand` is a compatibility candidate, not a guaranteed solution.** Synthetic `beforeinput`, `input` or `paste` events are not trusted actions and should not be assumed to trigger the editor's native handling.
5. Build a **small reproducible test matrix** in our real Lexical and Draft.js fixtures comparing ordinary typing/pasting with each extension-accessible candidate. Record: exact operation, app internal state, DOM result after reconciliation, caret, existing content, Undo/Redo, failure classification and browser version. Prefer editor-agnostic behavior that works in both frameworks; document any unavoidable differences.
6. **Only then implement** the narrowest validated shared insertion strategy in `extension/text-insertion.js`, preserving the current safe rejection for unsupported multiline cases and explicit recovery until the corresponding tests pass. Keep site-specific X/ChatGPT/Claude adapters out of this Issue unless a separately reproduced production-specific defect justifies a follow-up.

### Investigation deliverable / acceptance

- [ ] Document the relevant Lexical and Draft.js source files/functions, upstream permalinks (preferably pinned versions), their normal multiline input/paste flow, and the exact reason our previous browser editing experiments fail.
- [ ] Document **which of those flows are actually triggerable from an unprivileged external content script**, not just what works when calling app-owned internal APIs.
- [ ] Record at least one repeatable comparison for each framework showing actual editor model state vs rendered DOM across an asynchronous re-render and Undo/Redo.
- [ ] If no safe general external route exists, report the limitation and retain the non-destructive rejection/recovery behavior rather than pretending the Issue is fixed. Only propose a focused fallback or subsequent Issue supported by the findings.

## Expected outcome

Support committed multiline dictation in these editors through a verified, editor-compatible operation that preserves application state, existing content, selection and Undo where supported. Keep editor-type-aware, site-agnostic handling and the separate authorization models of website microphone dictation and FocusedInputTextOutputNode. Do not replace the safety guard with blind DOM mutation, synthetic trusted keyboard events or automatic replay after ambiguous edits.

Pre-merge acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Reproduce the current limitation with the real Lexical and Draft.js fixtures in `tests/fixtures/rich-editors/editors.js` and `tests/extension/text-insertion.spec.js`: select `world` in `hello world`, insert `voice`, then two ` voice` segments, then `\nnext`. Currently the last segment returns `not-inserted` and the editor remains `hello voice voice voice`.
- [ ] Verify successful multiline insertion into both real framework models after asynchronous reconciliation and a subsequent application render. Include insertion at the caret, selected-range replacement, existing multiline content, repeated committed segments, manual edits and Undo/Redo.
- [ ] Exercise the shared behavior through both authorized output routes; preserve bounded ordered recovery, no duplicate replay, focus/target safety, composition handling and healthy recording on delivery rejection. Unsupported or ambiguous outcomes must retain text safely.
- [ ] Run the affected browser suites and relevant unit regressions. Update the compatibility evidence and remove or narrow the rejection guard only for validated behavior.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Acceptance uses automated local fixtures and does not require logged-in sites or human sign-off.

## Context

Parent: #375. Partial implementation: #376. Current guard: `extension/text-insertion.js`; evidence: `docs/evidence/web-voice-375.json`. This follow-up covers the known multiline incompatibility; it does not claim any reproduced production-site failure or require site-specific adapters.
